subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [3:691] “Insured vs. insured” exclusion: D&O policies typically exclude coverage for actions brought by one insured director or officer against another (usually excepting shareholder derivative suits). For example: — “In consideration of the premium charged, it is hereby agreed that the Insurer shall not be liable to make any payment for loss … under this policy in connection with any claim or claims made against the Insureds by an Insured as defined in this policy, including the Company … except for stockholders' derivative actions brought by a shareholder of the Company other than an Insured.” [See Conklin Co., Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. (D MN 1987) 1987 WL 108957, *1 (emphasis added)] [3:691.1 - 3:691.4] Reserved. (1) [3:691.5] Purpose: One purpose of the insured vs. insured exclusion is to prevent collusive suits by corporations trying to recoup corporate losses by attributing them to the wrongdoing of directors and officers who, if insured, have nothing to 4 lose by taking the blame.
